purpose: Intense sweetener used in place of sugar in 'diet', 'light' and sugar-free products.
hazard_summary: Must be avoided by people with phenylketonuria (PKU) because it is a source of phenylalanine. In 2023 IARC classified aspartame as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2B, limited evidence) while JECFA kept its acceptable daily intake unchanged.
evidence_limitations: IARC hazard classification (limited evidence) is not a risk estimate; JECFA/EFSA risk assessments concluded intakes within the ADI are not of concern. Seed record: needs human review against the cited documents.
permitted_use_notes: Permitted additive in many jurisdictions under conditions of use; check local rules.
precautions: People with phenylketonuria should avoid phenylalanine sources, including aspartame, and follow their clinician's guidance.

purpose: Antimicrobial preservative, mainly in acidic foods and beverages.
hazard_summary: Evaluated together with benzoic acid and other benzoates as a group. Hypersensitivity-type reactions have been reported in some sensitive individuals.
evidence_limitations: Seed record: sensitivity claim and group ADI must be checked by a reviewer against the cited opinion. Benzoate effects in combination with certain colours were examined in other EFSA work not cited here.
permitted_use_notes: Group of benzoates evaluated together; use conditions vary by food category and jurisdiction.
precautions: People with a documented sensitivity to benzoates should check labels and seek clinician advice.

purpose: Preservative and colour fixative in cured meats; inhibits growth of Clostridium botulinum.
hazard_summary: At high doses nitrite can cause methaemoglobinaemia (reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of blood); infants are more susceptible. Under conditions that favour endogenous nitrosation, ingested nitrite is classified by IARC as probably carcinogenic to humans (Group 2A).
evidence_limitations: Seed record: the cancer classification applies to conditions favouring nitrosation, not to every exposure. Verify wording against IARC and EFSA documents.
permitted_use_notes: Use is regulated with maximum levels in many jurisdictions.
precautions: Follow paediatric guidance for infants; seek urgent care for blue-grey skin, breathlessness or collapse after a suspected high nitrite exposure.

hazard_summary: In 2021 EFSA concluded it could no longer consider E171 safe as a food additive because a genotoxicity concern could not be ruled out. Its EU authorisation as a food additive was subsequently withdrawn.
evidence_limitations: EFSA's concern relates to uncertainty about genotoxicity of nanoparticles; no safe intake level was established, so no numerical limit is recorded. Regulatory status differs between jurisdictions.
permitted_use_notes: Not authorised as a food additive in the EU; status elsewhere varies, verify locally.
precautions: Individuals who prefer to avoid it can check labels for E171 / titanium dioxide.
